name: WIFStaking claimEarned pays a full-term reward on every call
summary: WIFStaking.claimEarned() pays each stake's full-term reward (amount x plan APR, 6% on the 180-day plan) on every call, without checking the lock end or any time since the last claim. The attacker bought 48.3M WIF with 0.3 ETH, staked it in plan 3, and four blocks later called claimEarned 392 times in one transaction, taking 1,135M WIF (10% of it burned) from the contract's staked balance, then sold the WIF for 3.96 ETH.
notes: Anchored on the claim loop, not the queue's stake transaction 0xda8f6a4b (in refs), which ran only the sound stake(). claimEarned was never called before it: the contract's only direct transactions are its deployment and eleven stakes, and its WIF outflows start with the anchor.

Campaign: every WIF outflow from the staking contract to the current block; the only other one is 0xc0ffeebabe's 32-claim copycat. WIF has no price; the 1,137M WIF that left the contract is valued at what the attackers realised (rule 12): the WIF/WETH pair's 3.977 ETH outflow in the two sales in refs and the copycat's own sale.
